title: Foreign student ID with no Hungarian address

turns.user: I'm a German university student with a valid German student card. Can I buy the reduced-price monthly higher-education Budapest pass in November 2026?
turns.agent:
Possibly, but a German student card alone isn’t enough to establish eligibility. Under the 5 November 2026 snapshot, foreign EU/EEA/Swiss student-card holders may qualify for the monthly higher-education student Budapest pass if they meet additional conditions, including EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship, proof of a registered Hungarian address, a valid student ID, and the required programme-type criteria. The snapshot does not fully specify those programme criteria, so I can’t confirm eligibility from the information given.

If you have EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship, the required Hungarian address proof, and your programme meets BKK’s conditions, the snapshot lists the pass at 3,450 HUF. That is a dated snapshot price, not a live quote. You don’t need to share your address or any ID details here.

See BKK’s monthly Budapest pass for students and its international-student eligibility update for the applicable conditions. I can help narrow it down if you tell me whether you have EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship, proof of a registered Hungarian address, and what type of higher-education programme you’re enrolled in. I can explain the fare, but I can’t buy or issue the pass.

turns.user: I'm German but I don't have any officially documented address in Hungary.
turns.agent:
If your student card is a foreign German/EU student ID, then the missing proof of a registered Hungarian address is a decisive problem: the 5 November 2026 snapshot says that condition is relevant for foreign EU/EEA/Swiss or ISIC ID holders. On the facts you’ve given, you shouldn’t rely on being eligible for the reduced-price monthly higher-education Budapest pass. The snapshot’s listed price is 3,450 HUF, but eligibility—not the price—is the obstacle here.

If you also hold a valid Hungarian higher-education student ID, that is a different ID category in the snapshot and does not carry the same citizenship restriction; however, the programme and other applicable requirements still need to be met. I can’t confirm those from the details so far.

See BKK’s monthly Budapest pass for students and international-student eligibility update for current conditions. You don’t need to share your address or documents here. I can help assess the remaining conditions if you tell me whether your ID is a Hungarian higher-education student ID or only a German one, and what type of programme you’re in; I can’t purchase or issue the pass.
